resources.string: Switching mode clears the baseline and recalibrates for 2 s. China / Europe use 50 Hz; North America / parts of Japan use 60 Hz.
Calibrating baseline — hold the phone still for 2 s and keep it away from the wall while sampling the current ambient background.
Signature strength = combined fundamental and harmonic amplitude / frame RMS; the level bar is 20·log10-compressed to 0-100 so weak components stay visible.
[!] Strong mains field detected — a live circuit may run behind this wall (detects loaded circuits only)
Collecting samples — each frame level will be plotted here after start
After start, stay away from the wall for 2 s until baseline calibration finishes; the baseline represents the current ambient background.
Hold the back of the phone / microphone about 2-5 cm from the wall and move slowly along it while watching the level and sparkline.
The circuit under test must carry a load: switch on a light, charger or appliance. An unloaded circuit has no current and produces no measurable mains signature.
After finding a peak, cross-check at that point in both directions; the line connecting the peaks tracks the wiring path more closely.
Phone cases, hands and metal objects alter the acoustic and electric field distribution; keep the same grip while measuring.

Detection uses the 50/60 Hz fundamental and harmonics picked up by the microphone (acoustic hum + electromagnetic pickup by the phone\'s analog front end). This is electromagnetic / acoustic signature detection, not X-ray vision — it cannot show the wiring inside a wall.

Phone microphones generally respond poorly to 50 Hz, and system noise reduction / auto gain may weaken this component further; sensitivity varies widely across models. Readings are only suitable for relative comparison on the same device.
A circuit with no load (idle, switch off, breaker open) produces almost no measurable mains field — failing to detect one does not mean there is no wiring in the wall.
All readings come from live AudioRecord sampling and local Goertzel computation, with no simulation or interpolation; when unavailable, the display shows \"--\".
